rules.rationale: Source ESOL value prior: smiles_short gave +6.89 effect; compact solutes carry low cavity-formation cost in water.
Source prior for smiles_mid was -6.61; added nonpolar bulk raises the hydrophobic penalty.
Strongest source value prior (-11.46) at smiles_long; large hydrophobic surface dominates unfavorable solvation.
Ring role had the highest field transfer weight (0.758); acyclic solutes are generally less hydrophobic than ring-rich analogs.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size and ring-structure effects to FreeSolv, assuming solubility and hydration share hydrophobic-bulk mechanics. Fails if hydration affinity is driven by polar hydrogen-bonding groups rather than molecular size.

rules.rationale: Abundant N/O centers give strong solute-water hydrogen bonding, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Heavily halogenated surfaces are weakly polar, hydrogen-bond poor, and incur large cavity costs in water.
Moderate polarity without halogens is the classic hydrophilic small-solute regime in aqueous solvation data.
Counter-hypothesis reversing the low-confidence ESOL size prior: longer chains often carry extra hydrating functional groups.

skills.hypothesis: Assumes hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity and penalizes halogenated hydrophobes, downweighting the uncertain ESOL size prior. Fails if the score instead rewards small nonpolar solutes.

state.lesson: Cross-property ESOL transfer carries low source confidence (0.16-0.41) and mostly field-level roles, so mechanistic hydrogen-bonding rules are a safer prior than borrowed size effects.

Selected the polarity skill; both decay semantic mass so target-only GP evidence dominates later rounds.
